thread:
Camille Ortiz: quick check-in: i'm drafting a refactor RFC to make the runtime token verifier pluggable so gateways can choose local-agent vs remote-policy. want thoughts on minimal surface.
Vikram Shah: pluggable verifier sounds good. surface = token schema + verifier interface + bundle lookup. keep gateway hot path: verify header, lookup cache, apply ACL.
Noah Reed: +1. important: interface must allow both: 1) local agent that holds bundles and verifies signatures, and 2) a remote call to policy svc for dynamic checks.
Camille Ortiz: exact fields i propose in token: iss, sub, rid (registry id), bv (bundle version), exp, ds (optional dataset hash). keep names short to reduce size.
Vikram Shah: example token payload OK. also add an `m` membership stamp for quick allowlist checks. e.g.: "m":"r12,r34".
Noah Reed: question on signing: should gateways verify every token signature? that adds CPU. maybe gateway keeps a session cache of verified token ids and only verifies new tokens.
Camille Ortiz: agree. session cache + LRU recommended. RFC should mandate safe defaults: session TTL <= token TTL, verification on new token or on signature-key rotation event.
Vikram Shah: for Private installs, agent mode must support offline bundle ingestion + periodic delta updates. token includes bv so gateway knows which bundle to consult.
Noah Reed: audit: gateway should emit decision events with `token_id`, `rid`, `decision`, `reason` asynchronously. give customers opt-in for sending logs back.
DevOps Bot: runbook note added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/verifier-pluggable (task: "smoke-test session-cache behavior").
Camille Ortiz: migration plan sketch: 1) token-adapter service issues ephemeral runtime tokens for legacy API keys; 2) gateways accept both legacy header and runtime-token for a grace period; 3) rotate long-lived keys out over 6-12 months.
Vikram Shah: we should also provide a lightweight SDK for on-prem agents that can validate bundles and serve as verifier plugin. keep the plugin API small (verify(token) -> decision + metadata).
Noah Reed: perf targets: hot path added latency <= 5ms (session-hit), signature verify on cold token < 10ms. i'll bench in staging.
Camille Ortiz: security note: tokens must be short TTL (5-15m) for hosted; private can choose longer but must enable revocation via rid mapping.
Vikram Shah: revocation semantics: update registry mapping to remove rid -> gateway sees mismatch and denies after bundle refresh. document eventual consistency and TTL windows.
Noah Reed: i'll add failure modes: bundle tamper (reject), stale bundle (deny or fallback to remote eval), session cache poisoning (limit size & verify on suspicious cases).
Camille Ortiz: action items: Camille RFC draft, Noah perf numbers, Vikram agent SDK sketch. sync Mon 9am.
Vikram Shah: I'll prototype the plugin interface and a tiny Go verifier by EOW.
Noah Reed: will run perf sims and attach numbers to the RFC. aiming for p99 budget under 30ms for full path.
Camille Ortiz: thanks all. keeping the verifier pluggable gives product flexibility for Hosted/Dedicated/Private while keeping gateway latency tight.
